key_idea: One step maps position i to s[2i mod n], so k steps give t[i] = s[(2^k * i) mod n]; just compute 2^k mod n by fast exponentiation.
sketch: Taking every second letter of s+s gives new[i] = s[2i mod n] for both parities of n, and composing k times multiplies the index by 2^k modulo n. Compute r = 2^k mod n with binary exponentiation (k up to 1e18) and output s[(i*r) mod n] for each i. O(n + log k). Pitfalls: n = 1 makes everything 0 mod 1, read k as 64-bit, and i*r stays below 1e10 so 64-bit arithmetic is enough.
